svg.title: Building an event game with a backup and a final version
svg.desc: A flowchart: lock the brief, build one shared core, make each product difference a scene switch, then split into a backup that runs only on hardware you control and a final that uses the venue's own hardware. Test each, package both, and on show day run the final if its hardware works, otherwise switch to the backup in minutes with no data lost.
svg.text: Backup + final: a recipe for event games
How FinRace shipped two versions from one codebase, so show day never depends on a single piece of hardware.
Lock the brief and the hardware
Who plays where (tablets, LED, buttons), how many at once, the venue network, and what data the client must keep.
Write down which hardware you control and which belongs to someone else: that line decides the backup.
Build one shared core
Game rules, scoring, the network protocol, data saving and every tunable value live once, in code and config files.
Make the race deterministic (same seed + same clock = same race) so any screen can mirror or run it.
Save registrations and results to disk before acknowledging them, so no version can lose a lead.
Make every difference a scene switch, not a fork
Each version gets its own scene folder with a few flags ticked (e.g. "registration only", "race on the LED").
Switched off, the code takes the original path, so improving the core improves both versions at once.
BACKUP: hardware you control
FinRace: players race on their own tablets;
the LED mirrors both races live over OSC.
Tablets + PC + router, nothing else.
FINAL: the venue's own hardware
FinRace: tablets only register players; the race
runs on the LED, played on an OSC button box
(left / right / jump per player), built by another team.
Finish it first, then freeze it
Get it approved end to end before the
final exists. After that, change it only
through the shared core.
It is your insurance policy.
Agree the contract, not the device
Publish the exact messages and port the box
must send. Accept several forms, ignore
repeats, log anything wrong.
Keyboard keys do the same job as a fallback.
Test the whole floor
Two tablets and the LED on one network:
registration, race, results, leaderboard,
a tablet closed mid-race, a lost Wi-Fi.
Test without the box, then with it
Simulate presses from any OSC app. Add an
on-screen monitor (IP, port, each press lit)
so staff can check the real box in seconds.
Package both, the same way
One menu click builds all four apps (2 tablet APKs, 2 LED exes) and two zips. Each zip has a setup script that opens
the UDP ports in the firewall, the apps, and a one-page guide. Both use the same data folder on the PC.
Optional: an end date baked into every build, for a licence that runs out after the event.
Show day: does the final's
hardware work on site?
Yes
No
Run the final
Tablets register, players race on the LED
with the buttons. The backup stays in the bag.
Switch to the backup in minutes
Install the other APK, start the other LED app.
Same tablets, PC, network and saved data.
Rule of thumb: never let a part you don't control be the only way the event can run.
